:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem: The function $B(s)$ models a school's budget, in dollars, given the average number of students $s$ in each grade. What is the best interpretation of $B'(30)=2\,000?$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
The function $B'(s)$ represents the rate at which the budget is changing at the moment when the school has an average of exactly $s$ students in each grade.

Therefore, $B'(30) = 2\,000$ means:

*When the school has an average of $30$ students in each grade, its budget is increasing at a rate of $2\,000$ dollars per student.*

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: The function $S(t)$ gives the area, in squared centimeters, of a thin sheet of ice as it melts $t$ minutes after observations start. What is the best interpretation of ${S}^{′}(5)=-7?$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
The function ${S}^{′}(t)$ represents the rate at which the area of the sheet is decreasing $t$ minutes after the beginning of the observation.

Therefore, since it is negative, ${S}^{′}(5)=-7$ means:

$\,$ *$5$ minutes after the observations began, the area of the sheet decreases at a rate of $7$ squared centimeters per minute.*

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
The function $P(v)$ models the price of lemonade sold at a lemonade stand, in dollars, depending on the volume $v$ sold the previous day, in liters. What is the best interpretation of the statement below?

$\,$ *The slope of the tangent line to the graph of $P(v)$ at $v=4$ is equal to $0.5.$*
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
The slope of the line tangent to the graph of $P(v)$ at $v=4$ gives the derivative of $P(v)$ at $v=4.$ So, we have that

$$
{P}^{′}(4)=0.5.
$$

We can interpret the above statement as

$\,$ *When $4$ liters of lemonade are sold the previous day, the price is increasing at a rate of $50$ cents per liter.*
